producer_report.summary:
Slice 1 is built. The design is amended for review 3's N1-N4, and a new tested library module, `crates/athena-core/src/pr.rs`, covers owned mode. Nothing calls the module yet: there is no command, no `gh` call and no stealth code. fmt, clippy and the full test run are clean.

Design changes (`docs/design/native-pr-landing.md`):
- **Status:** the line no longer says "Not yet re-reviewed". It cites review 3, and a revision note lists N1-N5.
- **N1:** the merged-content check computes the governed-content fingerprint of the merged commit and compares it with the verified fingerprint. I dropped the diff branch. A merged-but-refused job is in the named state `merged-unverified`. The user leaves that state by re-verifying the job on the new tip as a new job.
- **N2:** the PR number, host, repository and pushed head live in a link file in the job's state directory, in both modes. The records schema does not change.
- **N3:** the stealth body keeps a plain description of the change and drops the job id and Athena vocabulary. The leak check covers the body and the branch name. Stealth pushes a neutral branch name. The push guard compares the pushed branch with the one name Athena chose and stored.
- **N4:** a stealth squash of several jobs runs five per-job checks over the local store: record validity, verdict and fingerprint, prediction order, chain, and secret scan.
- **N5:** a one-line wording fix in step 5, plus a note on path style.
- **Enforcement table:** the §8 enforcement table gains three rows.

Module (`pr.rs`, registered in `lib.rs`):
- **Link store:** `PrLink`, `store_link` and `load_link`, under the job's state directory (`pr-link.json`), outside `records/`. The link also carries a state (`Open`, `Landed`, `MergedUnverified`) and the merged commit id.
- **Push guard:** `check_push` refuses any branch other than the allowed one. It also refuses a remote head that is not an ancestor of the pushed commit, including one git does not know. It has no force option.
- **Merged-content check:** `check_merged` takes a `Host` trait and a `Content` trait. It finds the merge by the stored PR number and never reads the merged commit's message. It returns `NotMerged`, `Verified`, or `MergedButNotVerified`. `apply_outcome` sets the link's state from the result.

Other docs: D86 in `docs/decisions.md`, a CHANGELOG entry, and a short update to the push row in `docs/enforcement.md`.

I did not touch `store.rs`, `paths.rs` or `roadmap.md`, which the deliverables list names. The module needed none of them, and changing the roadmap order is out of scope.

checks_run.note: ran before the final fmt; no code changed after
ran with -q, the same tests. All suites passed, including the 5 new pr:: tests.

open_issues: clean_job deletes the link file with the job directory. The later command slice must keep the link until the merge is observed, or move it elsewhere. D86 records this.
The verified fingerprint is passed in by the caller. Nothing yet loads it from the job's records.
The neutral branch name is stored by the design, but the code does not generate it; that is for the stealth slice.
The design's claim that the neutral branch name is checked for job ids and Athena vocabulary is a later-slice mechanism with no test yet.
The records/ and state layout were not read in depth, so the link file's home (the job_dir) is a choice. store.rs and paths.rs did not need changes.
mistakes: The first test draft called commit_tree with three arguments and did not compile. I fixed it.
GitContent first lacked a Debug derive, which the workspace lint warns about. I fixed it.
learnings: The fingerprint (athena_git::attrs::fingerprint) is a SHA-256 over governed paths under the rules at a given commit, not a raw tree id. Merged-content equality must use it, because records/ differs in owned mode.
StateDir::clean_job removes the whole job directory, so a link file there is deleted at cleanup.
Git::commit_tree takes a fourth bool argument (sign).
The test utilities in athena-git (`testutil`) are `pub(crate)` and `cfg(test)`, so core tests build their own repositories.
Docs that name `/home/...` style paths or the listed boundary words fail the scan; I avoided them.
desires: A way to read the full output of a large cargo test run. The saved output was outside the working directory, so I could not search it and re-ran with -q instead.
A shared git test-utility crate, so core tests do not each rebuild their own repository helpers.
